name: The Setai
positioning: Oceanfront Miami Beach hotel in an Asian Art Deco building that first opened in 1937, with Ocean Suites in a modern high-rise tower
best_for: Travelers who want an oceanfront South Beach stay with three pools and a private stretch of beach
Diners interested in South Asian and contemporary Japanese cuisine

facts.text: The Setai's Asian Art Deco building was designed by architect Henry Hohauser.
The building originally opened as the Dempsey-Vanderbilt hotel in 1937.
The hotel has an oceanfront location at Collins Avenue and 20th Street in Miami Beach.
The Ocean Suites are located in a modern high-rise tower.
Ocean Suites stays include round-trip transfers between the Miami or Fort Lauderdale airports and ports.
The Pool Villas sit above the Spa Building on the second floor.
Suites have handmade Swedish Duxiana king-sized beds.
Accessible Art Deco Studio Suites have ADA-compliant features such as accessible showers, toilets and sinks.
Jaya serves Indian, Chinese, Thai and Balinese dishes in an indoor dining room and an open-air courtyard.
Japón serves contemporary Japanese cuisine with an extensive sake selection.
Jet Skis are available to rent.

highlights.text: The hotel has three infinity pools, each kept at a different temperature.
The hotel has its own private stretch of beach with day beds.
The nightly Asian Night Bazaar in the open-air courtyard features live performances by aerialists and contortionists.
The Penthouse spans the entire 40th floor atop the Ocean Suites tower and has a private rooftop pool with city and beach views.
Ocean Grill is an open-air beachfront restaurant serving Mediterranean-Italian lunch and dinner.

considerations.text: Ocean Drive is about 2 miles from the hotel, around 13 minutes by car.
Luggage storage is not offered on the property.
A casual elegant dress code applies at Jaya.
